risks.description: Technology risk is the potential for technology failures or shortfalls to disrupt a business or cause losses. It can involve information security incidents, cyber attacks, service outages, project failures, or uncertainty about technological development. Technology risk management is a part of enterprise risk management that aims to anticipate and mitigate potential problems.
risks.title: Technology

risks.description: Data risk is the potential for a loss related to your data. The term applies to failures in the storage, use, transmission, management and security of data.
risks.title: Data

risks.description: Third-party risk is the potential risk that arises from relying on outside parties, such as vendors, suppliers, partners, or service providers, who have access to internal or customer data, systems, processes, or other privileged information. Third-party risk can lead to adverse events, such as data breaches, operational disruptions, reputational damage, legal and regulatory violations, or fines and fees. Third-party risk management is the practice of identifying and minimizing the risks posed by third parties, especially in terms of cybersecurity.
risks.title: Third Party

risks.description: People Risk' in the context of Operational Risk is referenced by the Basel Committee as one of the key Operational Risk category of events being 'the risk of loss resulting from inadequate or failed internal processes, people and systems or from external events'.
risks.title: People

risks.description: Strategy implementation is the process by which an organisation translates its chosen strategy into action plans and activities, which will steer the organisation in the direction set out in the strategy and enable the organisation to achieve its strategic objectives.
risks.title: Strategy Implementation

risks.description: Environmental risk is the probability and consequence of an unwanted accident. Because of deficiencies in waste management, waste transport, and waste treatment and disposal, several pollutants are released into the environment, which cause serious threats to human health along their way.
risks.title: Enviromental

risks.description: This risk can be defined as the exposure to adverse consequences stemming from population-based activities and negative public perception. In other words, social risk is a manifestation of what goes on around us and is driven by influences inside every one of us—beliefs, emotions, mental health, fears and anxieties.
risks.title: Social

risks.description: Governance risk is the uncertainty about the consequences of an activity or event with respect to the rules, practices, and standards that guide a business. Governance risk is part of the broader concept of governance, risk, and compliance (GRC), which is the collective set of procedures that help organizations maintain their integrity and address uncertainty with respect to their business objectives. Governance risk can be managed by providing control mechanisms, policies, and procedures that align organizational activities and capabilities with business goals.
risks.title: Governance

risks.description: Regulatory risk is the risk that a change in laws and regulations will materially impact a security, business, sector, or market. A change in laws or regulations made by the government or a regulatory body can increase the costs of operating a business, reduce the attractiveness of an investment, or change the competitive landscape in a given business sector. In extreme cases, such changes can destroy a company's business model.
risks.title: Legal & Regulatory

risks.description: Legal risk indicates potential legal actions against a company. In contrast, compliance risk results in material loss and financial forfeiture. A lawsuit is an example of a legal risk. Whereas failing to deliver or comply with government regulations is a compliance risk. Legal risk is a broad niche and can sometimes overlap with compliance issues.
risks.title: Legal & Conduct

risks.description: Financial risk refers to the possibility of losing money on an investment or business venture. There are several types of financial risks, including credit risk, liquidity risk, and operational risk. Financial risk can result in the loss of capital for individuals, businesses, and even financial markets. For businesses that use borrowed money, financial risk is the potential losses incurred by investors when investing in the business. The more debt a company has, the higher the potential financial risk.
risks.title: Financial

risks.description: Process risk is a loss in revenue as a result of ineffective and/or inefficient processes. Ineffective processes hamper the achievement of the organization's objectives, whereas the processes that are inefficient, may be successful in achieving objectives, yet fail to consider high costs incurred.
risks.title: Process

risks.description: The inability to meet every day financial obligations
risks.title: Liquidity

risks.description: Non-compliance with tax obligations could result in regulatory censure or financial detriment
risks.title: Tax

risks.description: Risk that the firm has weak defences or is complicit in aiding money laundering activity leading to fines, censure and reputational damage.
risks.title: AML

risks.description: Risk that the firm has weak defences or is complicit in aiding fraudulent activity leading to financial Loss,  fines, censure and reputational damage.
